chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, raising it from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
I asked him about having intercourse with women in their hindquarters (anal sex), so he said, 'There is no harm in it, but I dislike that you do it.'
And the report which we presented earlier from al-Rida (peace be upon him), and his saying 'We do not do that,' indicates its dislike according to what we have presented earlier.
And it is possible that the two reports came in the context of taqiyya (dissimulation), because among the Sunnis, only Malik agrees with this, so it is permissible that they came in this manner.

key_terms.إِتْيَانُ النِّسَاءِ فِي أَعْجَازِهِنَّ: Having intercourse with women in their hindquarters (anal sex)
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: The general public (often referring to Sunnis in this context)
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on anal intercourse with one's wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the permissibility of anal intercourse with one's wife, with the Imam stating it is permissible but disliked (*makruh*). The text highlights a potential scholarly nuance by suggesting that reports of dislike may reflect *taqiyya* (dissimulation), as this practice was not widely accepted among Sunni jurists except for Malik. This context underscores the distinct Shia jurisprudential stance while acknowledging the historical interplay with broader Islamic legal traditions.
